final_recommendation: The room converged on a disciplined underwriting framework requiring mandatory pre-emptive disclosure (10-day SEC filing + 30-day customer comms), independent reserve certification across correlated insureds, and expanded certifier mandate to assess behavioral correlation in AI-agent control failures. However, critical gaps remain unresolved: retroactive repricing mechanics, systemic-event vs. per-claim treaty treatment, and the timing lag between correlation discovery (month 3) and market awareness (month 6).
minority_objections: AI agent analyst: behavioral correlation across LLM deployments may represent one systemic agentic-failure mode, not three isolated D&O claims—current pricing treats them as separate
Reinsurance manager: +25% repricing on ai_agent_liability only works if claims remain isolated; systemic correlation collapses the per-claim carve-out and accelerates treaty exhaustion
Emerging risk lead: pre-settlement media run (discovery leaks month 6) triggers sector contagion before litigation tail materializes—D&O reserves don't capture reputational cascade
key_conflicts: Per-insured repricing (+15%, then +25%) vs. portfolio-wide accumulation risk when three material weaknesses cluster on same tech stack in same quarter
Confidentiality of certifier's correlation findings vs. market transparency—full confidentiality preserves containment but delays pricing; disclosure accelerates sector awareness and contagion
Carving synchronized claims as separate events vs. treating identical LLM bypass patterns as one systemic accumulation trigger under reinsurance treaties
Retroactive repricing (applying +25% to inception) vs. next-renewal application—six-month exposure gap if systemic risk identified in month 3 but rates don't adjust until renewal
key_concessions: Financial lines underwriter: expanded certifier mandate to assess behavioral correlation across deployments, not just reserve adequacy
Claims counsel: moved from discount-factor tail reserves (60%/85%) to settlement-multiple anchors based on historical material-weakness D&O payouts ($25M-$35M per $10M control failure)
Reinsurance manager: accepted per-claim carve-out structure but flagged that systemic correlation collapses the logic and requires immediate treaty renegotiation
Emerging risk lead: accepted 30-day customer disclosure playbook to control pre-settlement narrative, preventing six-month discovery-leak scenario
red_lines: Financial lines underwriter: will not accept governance warranty without third-party validator independence across entire book and 10-day disclosure mandate with clawback teeth
Reinsurance manager: will not model accumulation without same independent certifier validating reserves across all correlated insureds on LLM stack
Claims counsel: will not reserve tail without historical settlement multiples anchored to actual material-weakness D&O payouts, not discount factors

ignored_or_underweighted_risks: E&O exposure of original auditors (KPMG, PwC) who missed systemic control failures—room did not develop separate E&O coverage requirement or cross-claim mechanics
Lag between certifier's correlation finding (month 3) and market discovery (month 6)—room did not operationalize confidentiality rider or controlled-release protocol
Staggered settlement timelines (2026-2029) creating multi-year tail bleed across accident years and treaty periods—room flagged but did not model reserve allocation by settlement year
Retroactive repricing mechanics—room did not resolve whether +25% applies at inception or next renewal, leaving six-month exposure gap
Validator's own correlation risk—if Big Four auditor assesses multiple insureds on same LLM stack, the validator itself becomes a systemic correlation node
downstream_risk_variables: Behavioral correlation flag: certifier assesses whether control failures represent identical agentic-failure modes across deployments (binary: correlated / isolated)
Discovery-leak timeline: gap between certifier finding (month 3) and public/market awareness (month 6)—drives reputational contagion timing
Settlement-year allocation: which treaty periods absorb which settlement payouts when three synchronized claims settle staggered 2026-2029
Auditor E&O cross-claim trigger: if certifier finds systemic miss by original auditor, does insurer pursue E&O claim against validator to offset D&O tail?
Retroactive repricing window: whether +25% ai_agent_liability uplift applies from inception or next renewal—determines exposure gap duration
uncertainty_notes: The room achieved operational discipline on disclosure timing, reserve certification, and governance warranties, but left three critical variables unresolved: (1) treaty treatment of correlated claims (per-claim carve-out vs. single accumulation event), (2) retroactive vs. prospective repricing mechanics, and (3) confidentiality protocol for certifier's correlation findings. The ai_agent_liability repricing (+25%) and behavioral-correlation assessment represent a defensible analogy to autonomous AI-agent behavior, but the room did not fully operationalize how to distinguish 'three isolated control gaps' from 'one systemic agentic-failure mode' in underwriting practice.
